insights.summary: H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to ₹91.5 Cr with EBITDA of ₹19 Cr (20.6% margin) and PAT of ₹13.1 Cr, helped by data centres (52% of revenue) and exports of ₹8.1 Cr. The executable order book is ₹307 Cr, enough for about two quarters. Management says it is on track for 35-40% growth for FY27 or better, with H2 generally double H1, and the new Ambernath plant's first dispatches slipped about a month to end-November.

what_changed.text: Ambernath phase one: first dispatches from end-November (earlier end-October)
FY27 growth of 35-40%, 'or bettering'; earlier conference note said about 50%
Order book ₹307 Cr (was ₹205 Cr in September); exports 22% of it
Acquired 99% of Mechtech Infrasolutions, a Siemens SIEPAN partner

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: Yes, we are absolutely on track.

analyst_questions.answer: Machines installed, first dispatches from end-November; phase one adds about 5,000 verticals, the rest comes with phase two.
H1 margin is diluted by fixed costs on a small half; H2 is generally double in revenue, so margins hold or improve.
₹11 Cr of IPO money in FD usable from April 2027, higher non-fund limits and better payment terms; unused bank limits available within 10 days.
ABB-branded share has come down and is being replaced by own-design products, which earn better margins.

red_flags.text: Operating cash flow was negative ₹55.5 Cr in H1; receivables of ₹119.8 Cr are larger than a year of H1 revenue.
Capacity utilisation is 95% at Navi Mumbai and Pune, so growth waits on the Ambernath plant, which slipped about a month.
Data centres are over half of revenue and 65% of FY26 revenue came from ABB-branded ArTu K panels.
Guidance given is lower than the 50% mentioned in July conference notes.

Receivables and operating cash flow improving
